newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba sees many reasons for investment outflow.
newsitem.headline: Buba sees many reasons for investment outflow.

text.p: German net capital exports from direct investment have surged in recent years for a wide range of reasons not exclusively tied to high business costs here, the Bundesbank said in its monthly report.

According to the central bank's August report, net capital exports from foreign direct investment have doubled from the second half of the 1980s and early 1990s when they amounted to between one-half to three-quarters of gross domestic product.

The Bundesbank found many reasons for the increase, but said an important factor was that German companies were investing more overseas simply because they wanted to increase their sales and distribution efforts.

"In theoretical and empirical investigations, sales-oriented motives were shown to be the main factor in decisions on direct foreign investment and the choice of investment locations," the central bank said.

The central bank said while strategic factors played a prominent role, more commonly cited reasons for capital outflow including high costs and the difficulty of doing business here also were factors.
The Bundesbank said high taxes, social payments and red tape made Germany a less attractive place to do business and said reforms that have already been proposed need to be acted on.
